title: Goal Decomposition
body:
This record covers Goal Decomposition within the Goal-to-Action Planning Database. Converts goals into executable action plans. The record is written as a complete, human-readable file: it states what the method is, when it applies, what it needs, what it produces, and where its limits lie.

How it works. Weighted decomposition: each goal is split into ordered actions, scored by importance and effort, then sequenced against deadlines. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the simple rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Scope and limits. This record describes established practice and workable designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how goal decomposition is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.

Further detail. This record also notes how goal decomposition is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.
demo_code:
# Goal Decomposition: weighted action-plan score
durations = [3, 5, 2, 4]
weights = [3, 2, 4, 1]
total_effort = sum(durations)
weighted = sum(d * w for d, w in zip(durations, weights))
print('actions:', len(durations))
print('total_effort:', total_effort)
print('weighted_score:', weighted)

title: Obstacle Anticipation
body:
This record covers Obstacle Anticipation within the Goal-to-Action Planning Database. Converts goals into executable action plans. The record is written as a complete, human-readable file: it states what the method is, when it applies, what it needs, what it produces, and where its limits lie.

How it works. Weighted decomposition: each goal is split into ordered actions, scored by importance and effort, then sequenced against deadlines. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the most-complex rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Scope and limits. This record describes established practice and workable designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how obstacle anticipation is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.

demo_code:
# Obstacle Anticipation: weighted action-plan score
durations = [3, 5, 2, 4]
weights = [3, 2, 4, 1]
total_effort = sum(durations)
weighted = sum(d * w for d, w in zip(durations, weights))
print('actions:', len(durations))
print('total_effort:', total_effort)
print('weighted_score:', weighted)
